campbell.title: Campbell City Council — September 15, 2026
campbell.summary: The Campbell City Council considered updates to the theater use policy, a cost-share agreement with the City of San Jose for resurfacing work, and the city's annual investment policy update for fiscal year 2026-27. The council also considered a budget adjustment to fund equipment replacement.
keyTopics: Proposed modifications to Council Policy Section 14 (theater use policy), effective September 16
Cost-share agreement with the City of San Jose, not to exceed $335,000, for resurfacing work
Annual update to the city's investment policy for fiscal year 2026-27
Budget adjustment to fund replacement of remaining equipment

saratoga.title: Saratoga City Council — September 16, 2026
saratoga.summary: The Saratoga City Council took up routine business along with two land-use appeals and final map approvals for property subdivisions. It also considered appeals of Planning Commission decisions on housing projects at 6th Street and Oak Place, and discussed options for law enforcement services ahead of upcoming town hall meetings.
keyTopics: Appeal of Design Review and setback variance approval for a house and ADU at 14650 6th Street
Appeal of Tentative Map and Design Review approval for a three-lot subdivision at 14486 Oak Place
Final map approvals for lot splits at 20517 Carniel Avenue and 19351 Saratoga Los Gatos Road
Discussion of law enforcement service options ahead of September 19 and 30 town hall meetings
Resolution amending the City's Conflict of Interest Code

los-altos.title: Los Altos City Council — September 22, 2026
los-altos.summary: The Los Altos City Council reviewed routine business including a wastewater treatment plant agreement, a VTA board appointment, and a legal services contract amendment, along with new appointments to several city commissions. The council also considered an interim urgency ordinance placing a temporary moratorium on new detention or custodial processing facilities in the city.
keyTopics: Interim urgency ordinance establishing a temporary moratorium on detention or custodial facilities and custodial processing facilities
Addendum No. 14 to the Regional Water Quality Control Plant agreement with Palo Alto and Mountain View
Councilmember Jonathan Weinberg's appointment to an additional two-year term on the VTA Board
Appointments to the Complete Streets, Environmental, and Planning Commissions
Amendment to the legal services agreement with Berliner Cohen, LLP, updating retainer and hourly rates

los-gatos.title: Los Gatos Town Council — September 15, 2026
los-gatos.summary: The Los Gatos Town Council reviewed routine business, including approval of minutes from prior meetings and the town's monthly financial and investment report for July 2026. The council also considered several contract-related items, including amendments to agreements for services and a heating, ventilation, and air conditioning agreement, along with new professional services agreements.
keyTopics: Monthly Financial and Investment Report for July 2026
Second Amendment to an existing agreement
First Amendment to the Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning agreement
New professional services agreements with outside contractors

san-jose.title: San José City Council — September 29, 2026
san-jose.summary: The San José City Council considered a mix of routine business and several airport, waste management, and infrastructure agreements at this meeting. Notable items included a proposed temporary moratorium on detention and custodial facilities on private and public property, a status report on the Measure T disaster preparedness and infrastructure bond, and a review of parking meter and garage rates and hours.
keyTopics: Temporary moratorium related to detention and custodial facilities on private and public property
Status report on Measure T (2018 disaster preparedness, public safety, and infrastructure bond)
Amendments to several airport lease agreements, including with Jett Pro Line Maintenance, PrimeFlight Aviation Services, and the General Services Administration
Review of parking meter and garage rates and hours
Conditional use permit and public convenience/necessity determination for Sakura Market at 184 South Market Street

mountain-view.title: Mountain View Council Sustainability Committee — September 29, 2026
mountain-view.summary: The Council Sustainability Committee reviewed a draft five-year plan for reducing greenhouse gas emissions community-wide, along with the latest data on how much the community emitted in 2024. Public comment was also invited on these and any other topics of interest to residents.
keyTopics: Draft Five-Year Community Decarbonization Plan
2024 Community Greenhouse Gas Emissions Inventory

sunnyvale.title: Sunnyvale City Council — September 29, 2026
sunnyvale.summary: The Sunnyvale City Council considered a mix of routine contracts and larger policy items, including a five-year plan to address homelessness in the city, upgrades to city technology and infrastructure systems, and a labor agreement adding pay for officers on a new Community Crime Reduction Team. The council also planned to recognize Filipino American History Month, Hindu American Heritage Month, and Domestic Violence Awareness Month.
keyTopics: Adoption of the Sunnyvale Homelessness Response Plan as a five-year framework, with a community outreach update
Contracts for city technology upgrades, including video conferencing/traffic management equipment, UPS power systems, and a computerized maintenance management system
A reimbursement agreement with VTA to relocate city water facilities for the US 101 Express Lanes project
A side letter agreement with the Public Safety Officers Association adding special pay for a new Community Crime Reduction Team
Adoption of city positions on state and local ballot measures for the November 2026 election

cupertino.title: Cupertino City Council — September 29, 2026
cupertino.summary: The Cupertino City Council met in closed session to conduct the performance evaluation of the City Manager, as allowed under state open meetings law. The public portion of the meeting consisted of a report on that closed-session discussion, with no other substantive city business listed on the agenda.
keyTopics: Closed-session performance evaluation of the City Manager

santa-clara.title: Santa Clara City Council — September 22, 2026
santa-clara.summary: The Santa Clara City Council approved environmental review, land-use designations, and a vesting tentative subdivision map for the proposed 408-unit University Station Residential project at 451-475 El Camino Real. Detachment of the San José parcel and final annexation still require separate approvals. The council also met in closed session on legal matters involving Silicon Valley Power and the California Department of Water Resources.
keyTopics: Public hearing on prezoning, annexation, and general plan land use designation for a 408-unit housing development at 451-475 El Camino Real
Review of the project's Environmental Impact Report (EIR) under CEQA
Vesting Tentative Subdivision Map approval for the same development
Closed session on existing litigation between Silicon Valley Power/Northern California Power Agency and the California Department of Water Resources
Closed session on anticipated litigation matters

milpitas.title: Milpitas City Council — September 15, 2026
milpitas.summary: The Milpitas City Council reviewed a draft plan for how the city will spend federal Community Development Block Grant funds, got an update on the red light camera traffic safety program, and discussed the condition of the Milpitas Community Center. The council also considered financial actions related to the former Redevelopment Agency, including a bond refinancing measure.
keyTopics: Draft Program Year 2025 Community Development Block Grant Consolidated Plan
Red Light Camera Traffic Safety Program update and authorization
Condition assessment of the Milpitas Community Center
Resolutions related to the Successor Agency to the Redevelopment Agency, including sale and issuance of refunding bonds

palo-alto.title: Palo Alto Parks and Recreation Commission — September 22, 2026
palo-alto.summary: The Palo Alto Parks and Recreation Commission reviewed proposed guidelines for using synthetic turf on playgrounds and discussed a park improvements ordinance recommendation for the Foothills Nature Preserve improvement project. The meeting also included a council liaison report, a department staff presentation, and updates from ad hoc committees and liaisons.
keyTopics: Proposed Playground Synthetic Turf Use Guidelines
Park Improvements Ordinance recommendation for the Foothills Nature Preserve Improvement Project (PE-21000)
Department staff presentation
Ad hoc committee and liaison updates
Council liaison report
